sections.html:
Work out which county holds your lot, because Kannapolis straddles the Cabarrus and Rowan county line. That answer decides who sends your tax bill and which courthouse office files your deed. Your last tax bill or the online parcel search will show it, and that county's tax office is the one to call.

The city has grown fast, from 42,625 residents in 2010 to 53,114 in 2020 and 61,708 in the 2025 estimate. That growth keeps buyers circulating, though new construction and older mill-era streets compete with your house when you pick a price. Owners usually choose between an agent, a sale on their own, and a cash buyer.

Owners live in about 65.6% of Kannapolis homes, and the midpoint home value is $276,400. Midpoint rent is $1,319 a month, midpoint household income is $73,836, and the city counts 22,509 households. Monthly owner costs sit at $1,603 for mortgage holders and $486 for owners with no loan. The average commute is 26.2 minutes.

Turnover is modest, since 89.2% of residents were at the same address a year earlier. These are citywide midpoints and tell you little about a single street, so check nearby sales and the county record for your parcel before you pick a price.

The oldest houses here date from the textile mill era. A small mill-era cottage, a subdivision house from the 1990s and a newer build near the research campus draw different buyers. If yours has an aging roof, original wiring or postponed repairs, an investor who takes it as is spares you the repair list retail buyers tend to send after inspection.

Shoppers include young families and research campus staff. About 22.3% of residents are under 18 and 14.5% are 65 or older, with 2.56 people per household, so family-sized homes with yards suit many of them.

Downtown is changing too. The city plans a farmers market and pedestrian and bicycle improvements in the old shopping district, and the research campus draws educators, researchers and health workers into the area. Houses within reach of downtown or the campus can appeal to that group, while commuters weigh the 26.2 minute average drive.

  • Families look for bedrooms, yards and school access.
  • Investors look at rents near $1,319 a month and at repair costs.
  • Campus and hospital employees look for short commutes.

Whichever county lists your parcel sends the bill, Cabarrus or Rowan. Cabarrus reappraises on a four-year schedule, tighter than the eight-year maximum in state law, and each parcel there carries fair market value as of January 1, 2024. A big jump between two reappraisals is no reason on its own to appeal.

Cabarrus County property tax calendar
WhenWhat happens
January 1The owner on this date is billed
JuneRates are expected to be settled
Late July or early AugustBills go out
September 1Bills are due
After January 5Bills count as late

County commissioners and the other taxing bodies set the rates. After a sale, the county asks the former owner to pass the bill along to the buyer. State law adds 2% interest in the first weeks after the grace period, then three-fourths of 1% for every month after.

Send your request for an informal review in writing to Cabarrus County Tax Administration and attach support, such as nearby sales or photos of defects. No particular format is required, though stronger evidence makes the review count for more.

An appraiser studies your material and answers with an Informal Review notice. If you still disagree, you have 30 days from that notice to move on to a formal appeal before the county equalization board, normally the commissioners themselves.

A lower assessment only saves you money while you own the house, though buyers can read the county card for any parcel. If your parcel is on the Rowan side, ask the Rowan County tax office for its revaluation schedule and appeal steps.

The deed goes to a register of deeds office, Cabarrus or Rowan depending on where the lot sits. The seller owes the excise tax, a dollar per $500 of price, with any fraction rounded up, paid to the office before it files the deed. A deed left unfiled exposes the buyer to lien creditors and later purchasers, so timing matters.

Recording carries a flat statutory fee, and filing a loan payoff is free. Your closing attorney will quote the exact figure for your documents.

The law sets the tax and fees, and your contract assigns each cost. Have your attorney or title office confirm your share before you sign.

sections.h2: If your mortgage is in default
sections.html:
Foreclosure here goes through a clerk's hearing rather than a full lawsuit, so a sale may still be possible while it plays out. The lender or trustee files a notice of hearing for the county of the property, and service has to happen at least 10 days ahead.

  • The clerk looks for a valid debt, a default, authority to foreclose and proper notice.
  • A judge hears an appeal of that finding if filed in 10 days, and a resident owner posts a bond of 1% of principal unless it is reduced.
  • After the auction, anyone may raise the price by at least 5% (minimum $750), and each raise restarts a 10-day window.

A payoff letter from your lender and a title search show how much equity remains, which you need before comparing offers.

sections.h2: Step by step: from offer to closing
sections.html:
1. Find your parcel number and county on your latest tax bill.
  2. Ask your lender for a payoff letter, and the tax office for any balance due.
  3. Gather written offers and compare what each one nets you after fees and repairs.
  4. Your closing attorney or title office searches title and prepares the settlement statement.
  5. Sign, and the deed goes to the Cabarrus or Rowan register of deeds. Taxes and liens are paid from your proceeds and you receive the balance.

A cash sale takes out the buyer-loan steps, so it often moves faster than a listing. Whatever route you choose, confirm the closing date and the condition the house must be in at handover before you sign.

Your answer turns on repairs needed, the calendar you face and the equity you hope to keep. Listing widens the audience and adds showings, repair demands and commissions. Buying for cash in present condition trades price for speed.

  • An agent makes sense for a polished home and an owner with patience for showings and loan approvals.
  • Go it alone only if you are at ease with pricing, disclosures and paperwork.
  • Cash fits when repairs, tenants, an estate property or a looming sale date rule out a long listing.

Insist on written offers, and have each buyer say who pays closing costs and recording fees.

faqs.a: Both. The city spans Cabarrus and Rowan counties. Your tax bill names the county for your parcel, so use that county's tax office and register of deeds.

faqs.q: Who owes the deed stamp tax on a Kannapolis sale?
faqs.a: The seller. It is one dollar for every $500 of the sale value, collected by the register of deeds when the deed is filed.

faqs.q: What is the Cabarrus tax due date?
faqs.a: September 1, and bills count as late after January 5. Pass the bill to your buyer once you have sold, since the January 1 owner is billed.

faqs.q: Can a Kannapolis house sell with back taxes or a defaulted loan?
faqs.a: Often yes. Your closing office pays taxes and liens from your proceeds, using payoff letters. With a foreclosure underway, the clerk's hearing and the upset bid window can leave room to close.

faqs.q: What does a typical Kannapolis home cost?
faqs.a: The midpoint value is $276,400. Your house will differ, so check nearby sales and the county card for your parcel.
